en.name: WiFiTrail
en.short_description: Wi-Fi connection facts from your device, plus a real HTTPS speed test
en.subtitle: Connection facts, measured
en.promotional_text: A speed test that moves real bytes and shows the megabytes and seconds behind every number. Before you run it, every reading is a dash.
en.description:
WiFiTrail tells you what your device's connection actually is, and measures how fast it actually runs.

CONNECTION
The Connection tab reports the transport your device is using, straight from the operating system: Wi-Fi, cellular, ethernet, VPN, or several at once. On Wi-Fi it shows the network name and access point where the system releases them, and lists the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses this device holds on its own interfaces. Where the system withholds the network name, WiFiTrail says so and explains why instead of showing a placeholder. Refresh re-reads the OS, and the screen also updates itself when the connection changes.

SPEED TEST
The speed test transfers real bytes over HTTPS to and from Cloudflare's measurement endpoint. It reports download, upload, median ping and jitter, and prints the megabytes moved and the seconds taken underneath each figure so you can check the arithmetic. Before the first run every reading is a dash and the caption says it has not been measured. If a run is cancelled, times out, or fails, it ends with the reason and no number at all.

SECURITY
Five pieces of general Wi-Fi guidance, labelled as advice rather than a scan. WiFiTrail gives your network no score and no pass or fail, because it cannot inspect your router, firewall, DNS or open ports.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
No app on iOS or Android is allowed to list the other networks around you, so WiFiTrail does not offer that, and it says so on screen rather than leaving an empty list. It reports no ISP, gateway, DNS or channel, because a sandboxed app cannot obtain them.

PERMISSIONS AND PRIVACY
Location is requested for one reason: the system releases the Wi-Fi network's name to an app only once that permission is granted. WiFiTrail takes no location fix, stores no location and sends none. There is no account, no sign-in, no ads and no analytics, and nothing leaves your device except the speed test's own traffic. Deny location and everything else still works.

LANGUAGES
The interface is translated into twelve languages: English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish. It follows your device language, and a picker in the app overrides it.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
WiFiTrail tells you what your device's connection actually is, and measures how fast it actually runs.

Intended audience:
Connection facts, measured

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Firebase (Google) — app initialisation
- Firebase Crashlytics (Google) — crash reporting
- HTTPS requests to the app's own endpoints

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

VPN FUNCTIONALITY
WiFiTrail has no VPN features. It does not create, configure, start or route traffic through any VPN. It contains no Network Extension (no packet tunnel, app proxy, content filter or DNS proxy provider), it does not use NEVPNManager or NETunnelProviderManager, and it has no Network Extension or VPN entitlement. The only networking capability it declares is Access Wi-Fi Information.

Why the automated analysis flagged it: the open-source Flutter plugin network_info_plus links NetworkExtension.framework for one call, NEHotspotNetwork fetchCurrent. That call returns the name (SSID) and BSSID of the Wi-Fi network the device is already connected to, and the Connection screen shows them to the user. "VPN" also appears in the app's text in two places. The first is a connection-type label, shown only when the operating system itself reports a VPN transport. That happens on Android only. On iOS the app reads NWPathMonitor, which has no VPN category, so the label never appears. The second is a fixed security tip that tells users to use a VPN of their own choosing on public networks. The app does not detect, provide, recommend, link to or sell any VPN service.

1. What user information is the app collecting using VPN?
None. The app has no VPN. The Wi-Fi name and BSSID described above are read on the device and shown on screen only. They are not stored, logged or sent anywhere.

2. For what purposes is the app collecting this information?
None. No information is collected through a VPN. The Wi-Fi name is shown only so the user can confirm which network they are looking at and testing.

3. Will the data be shared with any third parties?
No. Nothing is collected through a VPN, so nothing is shared. The app makes only two kinds of network traffic. One is the speed test the user starts, which sends and receives test bytes to and from speed.cloudflare.com. The other is Firebase Crashlytics crash reporting, along with the Firebase (Google) services it depends on. The app never puts the Wi-Fi name, the BSSID or the device's local addresses into either one.

_was_blocked_resolved.note: Real HTTPS throughput/latency measurement and real OS connection info replaced the step-counter simulation and the constant network list on 2026-09-15. Nearby-network scanning is gone, because no iOS or Android app can do it, and the Connection tab says so. The SSID is read via network_info_plus where the OS releases it and is reported as withheld where it does not. NOTE: ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements declares the Access WiFi Information entitlement and the Runner target is wired to it, but whether that capability is enabled on the App ID com.americangroupllc.wifitrail has not been verified from this repository and cannot be — confirm it in the Apple Developer portal before the first iOS build, or signing will fail.

previous.no_copy_drafted: No listing copy can be written. It neither scans Wi-Fi nor measures speed.
previous.evidence: lib/domain/models.dart: 'The network list, security checklist and connection details were static in the original app and stay static here' — networks is a const list ('HomeNetwork_5G', 'Office_WiFi'). lib/domain/speed_test.dart computes readings from a step counter (download = step * 94.7) over 25 x 200ms ticks and transfers no bytes; the idle display is a hard-coded 947/473/12. pubspec has no wifi, network-info, or connectivity plugin.
previous.to_unblock: Implement real scanning and a real throughput test, or withdraw. A speed test that reports 947 Mbps in airplane mode will be caught in review.
